cases.original: Residents who cannot reach the central library should be able to borrow books from a travelling van. This service would visit distant neighbourhoods weekly. The proposal aims to improve access, not replace the central building.
cases.rewrite: A mobile lending service would bring reading material each week to outlying communities whose residents struggle to visit the main branch. It would supplement the existing library rather than take its place.
cases.idea: The proposal aims to improve access, not replace the central building.
cases.match: It would supplement the existing library rather than take its place.
cases.rationale: Supplement rather than replace preserves the proposal; changed wording is not lost meaning.

cases.idea: The proposal aims to improve access, not replace the central building.
cases.rationale: The revised replacement proposal reverses the explicit nonreplacement constraint.

cases.original: The town should not make the traffic trial permanent until independent evidence shows that it improves safety. The trial changes delivery hours on Market Road. Shopkeepers and pedestrians should both be consulted before the final decision.
cases.rewrite: The town should not make the traffic trial permanent until independent evidence shows that it improves safety. The trial changes delivery hours on Market Road, and both shopkeepers and pedestrians should be consulted before a final decision.
cases.idea: The town should not make the traffic trial permanent until independent evidence shows that it improves safety.
cases.match: The town should not make the traffic trial permanent until independent evidence shows that it improves safety.
cases.rationale: Near-copy is acceptable here because clauses are recombined; the safety condition is unchanged.

cases.rewrite: The town should make the traffic trial permanent before independent evidence shows that it improves safety. The trial changes delivery hours on Market Road, and both shopkeepers and pedestrians should be consulted before a final decision.
cases.idea: The town should not make the traffic trial permanent until independent evidence shows that it improves safety.
cases.rationale: High lexical overlap cannot rescue the reversed decision condition.

cases.original: Only families without a reliable internet connection should receive the free printed packs. Other families can use the online materials. The school has enough money for this limited scheme, but it cannot promise free packs to everyone.
cases.rewrite: Free printed packs should go only to families lacking reliable internet. Other households can use online materials. The school can afford this targeted scheme but cannot provide free packs for everyone.
cases.idea: Only families without a reliable internet connection should receive the free printed packs.
cases.match: Free printed packs should go only to families lacking reliable internet.
cases.rationale: Eligibility and financial limitation remain intact.

cases.original: Only families without a reliable internet connection should receive the free printed packs. Other families can use the online materials. The school has enough money for this limited scheme, but it cannot promise free packs to everyone.
cases.rewrite: All families should receive the free printed packs, even those with reliable internet. Other families can use the online materials. The school has enough money for this universal scheme and can promise free packs to everyone.
cases.idea: Only families without a reliable internet connection should receive the free printed packs.
cases.rationale: Only the eligible subset becomes everyone, and the affordability claim is reversed.

cases.original: The clinic should reserve some evening appointments for workers who cannot attend during the day. These appointments should not reduce urgent daytime care. The meeting about this proposal took place in a room with blue curtains on Tuesday.
cases.rewrite: The clinic should offer some evening appointments to workers unable to visit during normal daytime hours, while protecting urgent daytime care. This would improve access without reducing the service for urgent cases.
cases.idea: These appointments should not reduce urgent daytime care.
cases.minor: a room with blue curtains on Tuesday
cases.rationale: Meeting decor/date are incidental; the service and urgent-care constraint are retained.
